reason: The text establishes and emphasizes multiple hierarchical relationships: (1) God's authority over humanity, demonstrated through explicit commands and prohibitions (וַיְצַו יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים - 'And the Lord commanded'); (2) Adam's authority over animals, shown through his naming of them ('whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof'); (3) Most explicitly, the male authority over the female, stated after the Fall: 'thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee' (וְהוּא יִמְשָׁל־ בָּךְ - 'he shall rule over you'). The woman is created as a 'helper' (עזר) for the man, further establishing a supporting relationship. These hierarchical structures are not merely incidental to the narrative but are integral to its moral and relational framework.
